# GNU.org
> Official home of the GNU Project and the Free Software Movement, promoting software freedom and developing the GNU operating system.

GNU.org is the primary source for GNU software, free software philosophy, licensing guidance, project history, manuals, package directories, and ways to participate in the GNU community.

## Start Here
- [The GNU Operating System and the Free Software Movement](https://www.gnu.org/): GNU homepage introducing the project, free software, and key site sections.
- [About GNU](https://www.gnu.org/gnu/gnu.html): Overview of the GNU operating system, its goals, and its history.
- [What is GNU?](https://www.gnu.org/gnu/thegnuproject.html): Introductory explanation of the GNU Project and its mission.
- [What is Free Software?](https://www.gnu.org/philosophy/free-sw.html): Defines free software through the four essential freedoms.
- [What is the Free Software Movement?](https://www.gnu.org/philosophy/free-software-even-more-important.html): Explains the social and ethical goals behind software freedom.
- [GNU Manifesto](https://www.gnu.org/gnu/manifesto.html): Richard Stallman’s original statement of purpose for the GNU Project.

## GNU Project and History
- [The GNU Project](https://www.gnu.org/gnu/thegnuproject.html): Background on GNU’s development, organization, and long-term objectives.
- [Initial Announcement](https://www.gnu.org/gnu/initial-announcement.html): The 1983 announcement describing the plan to build GNU.
- [GNU Manifesto](https://www.gnu.org/gnu/manifesto.html): Foundational essay describing why GNU was created.
- [GNU and Linux](https://www.gnu.org/gnu/linux-and-gnu.html): Explains the relationship between GNU and the Linux kernel.
- [GNU Name and Logo](https://www.gnu.org/graphics/agnuhead.html): Information about GNU’s name, symbolism, and visual identity.
- [GNU Timeline](https://www.gnu.org/gnu/gnu-history.html): Historical milestones in the GNU Project and free software movement.

## Philosophy and Free Software
- [Philosophy of the GNU Project](https://www.gnu.org/philosophy/philosophy.html): Central index of essays on freedom, ethics, and software policy.
- [What is Free Software?](https://www.gnu.org/philosophy/free-sw.html): Canonical definition of free software and user freedoms.
- [Why Open Source Misses the Point](https://www.gnu.org/philosophy/open-source-misses-the-point.html): Distinguishes free software values from open source framing.
- [Free Software Is Even More Important Now](https://www.gnu.org/philosophy/free-software-even-more-important.html): Modern argument for software freedom in everyday computing.
- [Copyleft](https://www.gnu.org/copyleft/copyleft.html): Overview of copyleft and how it preserves software freedom.
- [Words to Avoid](https://www.gnu.org/philosophy/words-to-avoid.html): Preferred terminology for discussing free software accurately.
- [Can You Trust Your Computer?](https://www.gnu.org/philosophy/can-you-trust.html): Essay on digital restrictions, control, and user autonomy.
- [The Free Software Definition](https://www.gnu.org/philosophy/free-sw.en.html): English version of the formal free software definition.

## Licenses and Compliance
- [Licenses](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/licenses.html): Main guide to GNU licenses, compatibility, and licensing resources.
- [GNU General Public License](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl.html): Overview and links for the GNU GPL.
- [GNU Affero General Public License](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/agpl.html): Overview of the GNU AGPL for network server software.
- [GNU Lesser General Public License](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/lgpl.html): Overview of the GNU LGPL for libraries.
- [Frequently Asked Questions about the GNU Licenses](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-faq.html): Detailed answers on GPL, LGPL, and AGPL usage.
- [License Compatibility and Relicensing](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/license-compatibility.html): Guidance on combining code under different free licenses.
- [How to Use GNU Licenses for Your Own Software](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/license-recommendations.html): Recommendations for choosing and applying GNU licenses.
- [Violation Reports](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-violation.html): Information on reporting possible GPL and LGPL violations.

## GNU Software Directory
- [GNU Software](https://www.gnu.org/software/software.html): Main directory of GNU packages and software categories.
- [GNU Packages by Name](https://www.gnu.org/software/software.html#allgnupkgs): Alphabetical list of GNU software packages.
- [GNU Package List](https://www.gnu.org/software/package-list.html): Structured package index with maintainership and status details.
- [GNU Alpha Releases](https://www.gnu.org/software/alpha/): GNU packages currently in alpha development.
- [GNU Download Area](https://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/): Official FTP archive for GNU source releases and distributions.
- [Savannah](https://savannah.gnu.org/): GNU’s primary forge for source hosting, issue tracking, and collaboration.
- [GNU Packages on Savannah](https://savannah.gnu.org/search/?type_of_search=soft&words=GNU&exact=0): Search interface for hosted GNU-related software projects.

## Manuals and Documentation
- [Documentation of the GNU Project](https://www.gnu.org/doc/doc.html): Central hub for GNU manuals, books, and documentation resources.
- [GNU Manuals Online](https://www.gnu.org/manual/manual.html): Index of official GNU manuals available on the web.
- [GNU Documentation License](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/fdl-1.3.html): Full text of the GNU Free Documentation License.
- [GNU Documentation Resources](https://www.gnu.org/doc/other-free-books.html): Collection of free books and documentation related to GNU.
- [GNU Texinfo](https://www.gnu.org/software/texinfo/): Documentation system used by many GNU manuals.
- [GNU Standards](https://www.gnu.org/prep/standards/): Coding, packaging, and documentation standards for GNU packages.

## Distributions and System Freedom
- [GNU/Linux and GNU](https://www.gnu.org/gnu/linux-and-gnu.html): Why GNU-based systems are often called GNU/Linux.
- [GNU/Linux Distros](https://www.gnu.org/distros/distros.html): Introduction to GNU/Linux distributions and GNU’s position on them.
- [Free GNU/Linux Distributions](https://www.gnu.org/distros/free-distros.html): List of endorsed distributions that respect user freedom.
- [Why Not Recommend Other Systems?](https://www.gnu.org/distros/common-distros.html): Explains why commonly used distributions are not endorsed.
- [Free System Distribution Guidelines](https://www.gnu.org/distros/free-system-distribution-guidelines.html): Criteria for systems seeking GNU endorsement.
- [GNU Packages in Debian](https://www.gnu.org/distros/common-distros.html): Context on distribution freedom issues and package inclusion.

## Education, Advocacy, and Campaigns
- [Education](https://www.gnu.org/education/education.html): Resources on using and teaching free software in education.
- [Take Action](https://www.gnu.org/help/help.html): Practical ways to support GNU and the free software movement.
- [Help GNU](https://www.gnu.org/help/help.html): Volunteer, donate, translate, test, and advocate for GNU.
- [Audio and Video](https://www.gnu.org/audio-video/audio-video.html): Talks, interviews, and recordings about GNU and free software.
- [GNU Kind Communications Guidelines](https://www.gnu.org/philosophy/kind-communication.html): Guidance for respectful communication in free software communities.
- [Malware in Proprietary Software](https://www.gnu.org/proprietary/proprietary.html): Catalog of harmful features found in proprietary software.
- [Defective by Design](https://www.defectivebydesign.org/): Campaign against DRM and digital restrictions, closely aligned with GNU values.

## Development and Contribution
- [How to Help GNU](https://www.gnu.org/help/help.html): Entry point for contributors, volunteers, and supporters.
- [GNU’s Who?](https://www.gnu.org/people/): Directory of GNU maintainers, volunteers, and contributors.
- [GNU Maintainers Resources](https://www.gnu.org/help/evaluation.html): Information related to package evaluation and GNU inclusion.
- [GNU Coding Standards](https://www.gnu.org/prep/standards/): Standards for GNU package development and maintenance.
- [GNU Webmastering](https://www.gnu.org/server/standards/): Standards and guidance for GNU web pages and site maintenance.
- [Translations](https://www.gnu.org/server/standards/translations/): Policies and practices for translating GNU web pages.
- [Savannah Help](https://savannah.gnu.org/maintenance/UsingGIT): Guidance for using Savannah infrastructure and Git hosting.

## News and Community
- [Planet GNU](https://planet.gnu.org/): Aggregated blog posts and updates from GNU contributors and projects.
- [GNU News](https://www.gnu.org/software/recent-releases.html): Recent GNU package releases and announcements.
- [GNU Press Shop](https://shop.fsf.org/): Books and merchandise supporting free software advocacy.
- [GNU Audio/Video Philosophy Recordings](https://www.gnu.org/audio-video/philosophy-recordings.html): Recordings focused on GNU philosophy and history.
- [GNU Events](https://www.gnu.org/server/events.html): Information about GNU-related events and participation.
- [GNU Mailing Lists](https://lists.gnu.org/): Mailing list service used by GNU projects and communities.

## Site Indexes and Reference
- [Site Map](https://www.gnu.org/server/sitemap.html): Structured index of major GNU.org sections and pages.
- [What's New](https://www.gnu.org/server/whatsnew.html): Chronological list of notable updates across GNU.org.
- [GNU A-Z](https://www.gnu.org/directory/): Directory of free software packages and related projects.
- [Search GNU.org](https://www.gnu.org/search/): Search interface for finding pages across GNU.org.
- [Accessibility Statement](https://www.gnu.org/accessibility/): GNU.org accessibility information and related resources.
- [Web Server Standards](https://www.gnu.org/server/standards/): Policies governing GNU.org page structure and maintenance.
